title: Fjord on-prem project sync (scratch)
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for Friday sync with Fjord ops/infra. Use as meeting prep + immediate follow-ups. Keep terse; copyable to a formal notes doc after the call.

Meeting logistics:
- Proposed time: Fri 11:00 PT (confirm with customer ops).
- Attendees (ask to confirm): Fjord infra lead (R. Ahmed), Fjord security (L. Park), Diego (solutions eng), Maya (sre lead), Oliver (release eng), me (Zoe).
- Goal: unblock IPsec tunnel jitter, finalize NAT/GW sizing, and agree on canary window for model rollout.

Agenda draft (20–30m):
1) Quick health read (3m) - Diego to report on current smoke tests and KV cache warmup success rate.
2) Network blockers (7m) - IPsec jitter, ephemeral port exhaustion, and NAT gateway allocation. Oliver owns NAT sizing proposal.
3) Prep for air-gap validation (5m) - checklist items, expected artifacts from customer. Maya to confirm runbook entry.
4) Rollout plan & canary policy (7m) - define traffic split, fallback, and metric thresholds. Zoe to propose canary window.
5) Action items & owners (3m).

Quick status snapshot (notes to read aloud):
- Deployment env: 4 GPU nodes (A100-40G equiv) provisioned in customer AZ1; 1 standby in AZ2.
- Model build: quantized variant v1.2-beta built and smoke-tested locally; failing intermittent memmap mount on node-3 during bootstrap (root cause suspected: stale systemd unit ordering).
- KV cache warmup: 82% success within 90s for canonical traces; latency tail (p99) still spiking with small bursts.
- Network: customer reports intermittent packet re-ordering causing IPsec SA rekey thrash; observed in their monitoring (see Jira PV-2541).
- Observability: sampling for kernel drops turned on, agent log level set to debug for 24h.

Detailed blockers (for discussion):
- IPSEC_JITTER: ongoing rekey loops when throughput > 800 Mbps. Impact: request timeouts on long-context generations; severity P1 for customer. Hypothesis: MTU mismatch + rekey timers too aggressive. Proposed short fixes: lower rekey freq on gateway, bump MTU to 9000 for internal path, enable offload options on customer NICs. Owner: Fjord infra + Diego.
- NODE3_BOOT: systemd start ordering causes /var/cache mount to race with inference runtime unit. Symptoms: memmap file missing -> process crash. Immediate workaround: systemd Override to add After=local-fs.target and ExecStartPre to touch file. Permanent: container entrypoint check + init hook. Owner: Oliver.
- NAT_CAP: current customer NAT gateway has 2500 ephemeral ports; expected to saturate at projected concurrency for warmup traffic. Impact: mid-rollout failures during heavy prefix cache fill. Ask: approve second NAT gateway (ha pair) or move to egress-proxy model. Owner: Oliver (proposal due Tue 2026-03-16).
- AIRGAP_ARTIFACTS_MISSING: customer has not provided signed image manifest + SBOM for on-prem air-gapped install. Blocks final validation. Owner: Fjord security (ask for ETA); Zoe to escalate if no ETA by Mon.

Proposed canary rollout (talking points):
- Canary window: 2 hours (09:00–11:00 local), traffic split 5% -> 20% over 3 steps with metric guardrails.
- Metrics to watch: 95th token latency, error rate (500s), model quality regression (sampled eval set BLEU/embedding-sim drop), CPU steal on nodes. Rollback triggers: >2x p95 or >0.5% increase in 5xxs sustained for 5m.
- Fallback: automatic traffic reroute to hosted fallback model (regionally compatible) if cluster-level health < 90% or NAT errors detected. Discuss SLA impact with customer.

Action items (flat list for copy/paste):
- "Diego: collect 3 representative generation traces that trigger p99 spikes and upload to Confluence (due 2026-03-09)"
- "Oliver: produce NAT sizing proposal with cost delta and egress topology options (due 2026-03-16)"
- "Maya: add explicit air-gap validation steps to runbook and mark which artifacts we still need from customer (due 2026-03-10)"
- "Zoe: draft canary playbook text and rollback triggers; circulate for +1 (due 2026-03-08)"
- "Fjord security (L. Park): provide signed image manifest and SBOM or ETA (requested by 2026-03-09)"
- "All: confirm attendee list and approve 11:00 PT slot (Zoe to send invite by EOD)"

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: NAT port exhaustion during cache warmup -> Mitigation: throttle warmup with token-bucket and stagger node warmup by 30s.
- Risk: IPsec rekey thrash causing timeouts -> Mitigation: tune rekey windows, enable jumbo frames on internal path, monitor for 6 hours at debug level.
- Risk: missing airgap artifacts -> Mitigation: temporary BYO-image flow (customer-run) while they finish validation; requires security sign-off.

Open questions to surface in meeting:
- Can Fjord ops enable jumbo frames in the internal path for test window? If not, who can network-engage?
- Does customer want a multi-NAT HA pair or an egress proxy model (prefers simpler infra vs cost)?
- Any constraints on escalation hours for rollback if the canary triggers at midnight for their region?

Notes-to-self / follow-ups after meeting (copy to official notes doc):
- Paste action items into Jira PV-2541 sub-tasks and tag owners.
- Create a short ops playbook gdoc with the canary steps + exact CLI commands for rollback; link in Confluence.
- Schedule a 30-min dry-run next Wed with customer to exercise warmup and failover. Propose Wed 2026-03-18 08:00 PT.

Scratchy timeline summary (for customer):
- This week: remove immediate boot race workaround on node3; toggle debug sampling; collect traces.
- Next week: finalize NAT sizing and canary playbook; customer to provide SBOM.
- Target production rollout: week of 2026-03-22 (contingent on artifacts and NAT decision).

Quick copyable closing line for meeting: "Primary ask today: confirm NAT decision (HA pair vs proxy) and provide SBOM ETA so we can lock canary window for next week."

-- end of scratchpad --
